cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Help Me Make This Normal
cards.instruction: Get someone to help perform the strange behavior until it feels ordinary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our invisible dinner guest is here. Introduce Mum while I finish the gravy, love.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't see where to look.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stand beside the guest's chair. Look towards me when you introduce her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Hello, chair, this is Mum. She needs your seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch Mum another chair. Introduce her to our guest, love.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs ordinary introduction to an invisible guest; A3 helps B locate the guest and A5 takes the seating job so B can complete the social ritual.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 inability to see earns A3 explicit chair cue; B4 Mum seat need earns A5 fetching another chair and redirecting the introduction.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs a location and B4 wants Mum seated, plausible hosting concerns despite the mistaken address.

heightening.evidence: A5 preserves guest status by solving Mum seating without evicting the invisible person.

specificity.evidence: A1 invisible guest, A3 guest chair and B4 Mum seat request supply all essential spoken context.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 practical chair offer and short corrected request replace the previous explanatory lesson.

coach2.stated: A1 guest is invisible; A3 points verbally to the guest chair and offers to stand beside it; B4 Mum needs a seat; A5 offers another.
coach2.inferred: B addresses the visible chair rather than its invisible occupant; the spoken cue explains the mistake.
coach2.firstDefect: The previously missing chair reference is now spoken in A3.

A1-B2.evidence: A1 introduction instruction meets B2 no visual target.

B2-A3.evidence: B2 visual problem causes A3 guest-chair orientation.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 chair cue leads B4 addressing the chair and requesting its seat.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 seat concern causes A5 extra chair and introduction to the actual guest.
